summary: Centralize documentation spaces and Slack ops provisioning into a single admin workflow
description:
Issue summary:
We want a single, auditable provisioning workflow that creates and configures new Confluence spaces for operational teams and the associated Slack channels with the correct permission groups and bot integrations. Currently team leads create spaces and channels ad-hoc which leads to inconsistent naming, missing audit metadata, and manual perms changes.

Impact:
- Fragmented knowledge base structure with duplicated spaces and inconsistent templates.
- Delays when spinning up new oncall teams (manual channel & space creation).
- Security overhead: missing groups or incorrect permission scopes for restricted spaces.

Request details:
1) Create a Confluence space template for "Ops Team" with required labels, page templates (runbook, playbook, postmortem), and space-level permissions that default to an "ops-readers" group and an "ops-admins" group.
2) Create a Slack provisioning automation (via our existing Jira -> Slack automation app or a new Automation rule) that, given a Jira form submission, will: a) create a channel with the naming convention #ops-<team>-<env>, b) invite ops-readers and ops-admins groups, c) install the standard set of bots (oncall-bot, incident-tracker), and d) post an initial pinned message linking the new Confluence space.
3) Define a Jira admin form (internal) that captures required metadata (team name, environment, primary oncall, channel visibility, space confidentiality level) and triggers both Confluence and Slack provisioning.
4) Add audit logging: every provisioning event should write a record to a tracked Confluence page and a Jira subtask for traceability.

Steps to reproduce / current manual flow:
- Team lead files a request in #support-ops Slack or in a freeform Jira ticket.
- Platform ops creates a new Confluence space, manually picks templates, sets perms, and emails the team.
- A second request is raised to create a Slack channel; platform ops repeats manual steps to create channel and invite members.

Proposed timeline and constraints:
- Prototype automation in staging within 3 weeks.
- Rollout to prod after one end-to-end dry run and sign-off from security and platform leads.
- Keep manual override path for confidential spaces.

Acceptance criteria:
- A Jira form exists to request both Confluence space and Slack channel in a single submission.
- Confluence space is created from the ops template with correct permissions applied automatically.
- Slack channel is created with naming convention, groups invited, bots installed, and initial pinned message linking Confluence.
- Provisioning events are recorded in a central audit page and linked Jira subtasks are created.
- Documentation and runbook created in Confluence for maintainers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Single Jira form can trigger both Confluence and Slack provisioning. 2) New Confluence space uses Ops template and default groups. 3) Slack channel created with #ops-<team>-<env> naming, ops groups invited, bots installed. 4) Audit entry created in central page and Jira subtask created. 5) Runbook exists and SRE sign-off obtained.
